STACKS LIBRARY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Robotic Process Automation (RPA) Project Documentation & Workflow Manual

A complete technical walkthrough of desk circulation, member management, and autonomous background robotic workflows.

System Type: Web-Based Desk Application with Integrated RPA Subsystem

Core Frameworks: Python Flask, SQLite, Robot Framework

Audience: Project Evaluation Committee / Viva Examination

Format: High-Contrast Monochrome Technical Specification

1. Project Scope & Overview

The Stacks Library Management System is an integrated college library desk application designed to eliminate manual, error-prone administrative tasks through Robotic Process Automation (RPA).

1.1 Problem Statement

Traditional library management involves highly repetitive manual interventions: tracking loan return deadlines, calculating overdue penalty fines day-by-day, sending individual warning emails to students, and auditing shelf inventory to identify depleted book copies. Manual handling leads to missed notices, inaccurate fine collections, and delayed stock replenishments.

1.2 Project Scope & Objectives

  • Core Desk Operations: Maintain full catalogue control (ISBN, author, title, category, copies), student membership records, and a formal lending desk workflow for book checkout and returns.
  • Role-Based Security: Strict multi-role separation among Admin, Librarian, and Student users.
  • Autonomous RPA Integration: Scheduled, headless software bots that autonomously monitor loan deadlines, calculate monetary fines, send email reminders, and audit inventory health without requiring continuous manual staff effort.
  • Dual-Log Audit Architecture: Total separation between bot execution telemetry (automation_logs) and human staff audit tracking (user_activity_log).

1.3 Technical Architecture

Component Technology Description & Purpose
Backend API Python 3.12 / Flask 3.1.3 RESTful endpoints, session security, business logic, fine calculations.
Database SQLite 3 (library.db) Relational storage: books, members, loans, users, automation_logs, activity logs.
RPA Engine Robot Framework 7.4.2 Autonomous bot test suites driving authenticated API workflows.
Notification Layer Python email_service MIME messaging with pluggable SMTP, Console, and Mock transports.
User Interface Vanilla HTML5, CSS3, JS Fast, responsive single-page desk interface with modal dialogs and live badges.

2. Written Workflow in Simple Language

The entire system operates through a sequential, logical lifecycle from initial book procurement to automated loan recovery:

Step 1: Adding Books to the Catalogue

A librarian or administrator enters book details (Title, Author, ISBN, Category, Total Copies). The system automatically validates the ISBN for uniqueness and initializes available copies equal to total copies.

Step 2: Member Registration & Activation

Students can self-register via the online registration form (/register). Alternatively, desk staff can register members in person. Staff-created members subsequently use the activation screen (/activate) to set their password and gain student portal access.

Step 3: Book Checkout (Lending Desk)

Staff select an available book and a registered member. The system checks copy availability, decrements available copies by 1, creates an active loan record, and automatically assigns a due date.

Step 4: Proactive Due-Date Monitoring (Courtesy RPA Bot)

Before any book becomes overdue, the automated Courtesy Due-Date Reminder Bot scans all active loans due within the next 24 to 48 hours. It dispatches a polite reminder email to the borrower, allowing them to return or renew the book before incurring fines.

Step 5: Overdue Detection & Fine Calculation (Overdue RPA Bot)

When a loan crosses its due date without being returned, the automated Overdue Reminder Bot triggers. It calculates elapsed overdue days, assesses an automatic penalty fine of ₹2.00 per day, records the result in the automation log, and sends an overdue warning notice to the borrower.

Step 6: Book Return & Fine Settlement

When the student returns the book to the desk, staff click "Return". The system increments available copies back by 1 and finalizes the fine amount. When the fine is settled, staff click "Mark Paid", clearing the student's dues.

Step 7: Automated Stock & Circulation Auditing (Inventory RPA Bot)

Staff run the Inventory Health Audit Bot to inspect catalogue circulation. The bot identifies completely depleted titles (0 copies available), flags low stock, computes utilization rates, and generates an automated Restock Advisory CSV file.

4. RPA Automation Features & Technical Deep Dive

This project incorporates dedicated Robotic Process Automation (RPA) workflows designed to execute both on-demand from the UI and autonomously in scheduled background routines via Robot Framework.

4.1 The Automation Centre (#automation)

Figure 4.1: Administrative Automation Centre with Bot Triggers & Status Feedback
Centralized hub where administrators can execute automated scans, observe live progress feedback, and trigger export routines.

Automation Feature 1: Daily Overdue Loan Detection & Fine Calculation Bot

Primary Function: Scans active borrowings where due_on < today, computes accrued overdue days, calculates penalties at ₹2.00/day, dispatches email reminders, and logs execution records.

Underlying Mechanism: Endpoint POST /api/automation/overdue and Robot Framework suite rpa/bots/overdue_reminder_bot.robot.

Fault Resilience: SMTP network failures are captured as [Email: FAILED] without crashing fine calculations or database logging.

Automation Feature 2: Advance Courtesy Due-Date Reminder Bot

Primary Function: Proactively scans loans due within 24 to 48 hours (due_on = today + 1 day) and dispatches courtesy advance notice emails before any penalty is incurred.

Underlying Mechanism: Endpoint POST /api/automation/courtesy and Robot suite rpa/bots/courtesy_reminder_bot.robot.

Database Logging: Appends directly to automation_logs with overdue_days = 0, fine = 0.0, and message tag [Email: SENT].

4.2 The Automation Log Interface (#automation-logs)

Figure 4.2: Granular Bot Execution History with Status Badges
Displays individual loan actions processed by the software bots, including member details, calculated fines, status tags, and email transmission indicators.

Automation Feature 3: Catalogue Inventory Health & Restock Advisory Bot

Primary Function: Performs an automated audit of the entire book collection, evaluating real-time inventory against borrowing velocity.

Key Metrics Computed:

  • available_copies vs total_copies.
  • utilization_pct: Percentage of copies currently in circulation.
  • Stock Status: Classified into CRITICAL_DEPLETED (0 available), LOW_STOCK (1 available), or HEALTHY.
  • Recommended Reorder: Suggested quantity of copies to purchase based on active borrow demand.

Deliverable: Generates an exportable replenishment advisory report at GET /api/reports/inventory-audit.csv.

Automation Feature 4: Daily Managerial Digest & Financial Reconciliation Bot

Primary Function: At the close of each operational day, aggregates total books issued, returns processed, fines assessed, outstanding balances, and active borrowings. Automatically compiles an executive summary digest and emails it to the library administration (LIBRARY_ADMIN_EMAIL).

Underlying Mechanism: Endpoint POST /api/automation/daily-reconciliation and Python email_service.send_reconciliation_digest_email.

Business Impact: Replaces manual spreadsheet end-of-day reconciliation with an automated, auditable financial digest.

Automation Feature 5: Unactivated Member Account Invitation Bot

Primary Function: Scans patrons registered at the desk whose online accounts have not yet been activated (account_active == 0). Automatically dispatches personalized onboarding invitation emails directing members to /activate.

Underlying Mechanism: Endpoint POST /api/automation/member-invitations and Python email_service.send_activation_invitation_email.

Business Impact: Streamlines student digital onboarding without requiring manual email correspondence by desk staff.

Automation Feature 6: Bulk Catalogue CSV Ingestion Bot

Primary Function: Replaces manual one-by-one book entry with batch data-entry automation. Parses uploaded CSV files, validates required attributes (Title, Author, ISBN, Category, Copies), gracefully skips malformed rows with diagnostic reasons, deduplicates by ISBN (automatically incrementing existing stock copies), and adds new acquisitions directly to the catalogue. Provides a downloadable standard CSV template for staff convenience.

Underlying Mechanism: Endpoints POST /api/automation/books/import-csv and GET /api/templates/books-template.csv.

Business Impact: Eliminates hundreds of keystrokes during new semester acquisitions and prevents duplicate ISBN conflicts automatically.

Automation Feature 7: Automated Circulation & Lending History CSV Export

Primary Function: Extracts all transaction history (book titles, members, issue dates, due dates, return dates, assessed fines, and payment records) directly into structured CSV (GET /api/reports/loans.csv) for audit archiving.

Automation Feature 8: Dual-Tier Separate Audit Architecture

Primary Function: Maintains strict separation between bot execution telemetry (automation_logs) and human staff audit tracking (user_activity_log), preventing log pollution and maintaining strict compliance auditing.

The system enforces strict multi-role permission gates via the @login_required decorator across all application views and API endpoints:

Feature / Endpoint Admin Role Librarian Role Student Role Unauthenticated
View Catalogue & Personal Loans Allowed Allowed Allowed Redirect to Login (401)
Add Books & Edit Catalogue Allowed Allowed Forbidden (403) Denied (401)
View Member Directory Allowed Allowed Forbidden (403) Denied (401)
Issue Books & Process Returns Allowed Allowed Forbidden (403) Denied (401)
Mark Fines as Paid Allowed Allowed Forbidden (403) Denied (401)
Run Inventory Audit & Download CSV Allowed Allowed Forbidden (403) Denied (401)
Bulk Catalogue CSV Ingestion & Template Allowed Allowed Forbidden (403) Denied (401)
Trigger Member Invitation Bot Allowed Allowed Forbidden (403) Denied (401)
Trigger Daily Reconciliation Digest Bot Allowed Forbidden (403) Forbidden (403) Denied (401)
Trigger Overdue & Courtesy RPA Bots Allowed Forbidden (403) Forbidden (403) Denied (401)
View Staff Audit Trail (User History) Allowed Allowed Forbidden (403) Denied (401)
View Automation History Logs Allowed Forbidden (403) Forbidden (403) Denied (401)
